q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
Let me work through this systematically.

## (a) Time left until resolution

Today is 2026-08-15. The question asks about Q2 FY2027 earnings release guidance. According to the research, NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 was released on May 20, 2026 (this is already in the past from today's perspective). This means the guidance has already been announced, and we're looking at approximately 2.5 months until the actual Q2 FY2027 earnings results would be finalized (typically late August/early September 2026).

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

The research explicitly states: **"NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue, released on May 20, 2026, predicts approximately $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%."**

This means the guidance range is roughly $89.2 billion to $92.8 billion. The most likely outcome is that the actual reported revenue for Q2 FY2027 will fall within or very close to this guided range.

The guidance appears to be the company's own forward-looking statement made on May 20, 2026, so by August 15, 2026, we have roughly 6-7 weeks of additional data/developments that could shift actual results relative to guidance.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- Weaker demand than expected in the data center market (NVIDIA's primary revenue driver)
- Unexpected supply chain disruptions
- Stronger-than-expected competition impacting pricing or unit volumes
- Macroeconomic deterioration reducing customer capex spending
- The guidance explicitly excludes China Data Center compute revenue, but any surprise reduction in non-China segments

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- Stronger-than-expected demand in AI/data center computing
- Successful new product launches or customer wins driving higher volumes
- Better-than-expected pricing power
- Potential upside from previously excluded China operations (though guidance specifically excludes this)
- Higher-margin product mix
- The company's strong momentum (Q1 FY2027 was $81.6B, up 20% sequentially)

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

From the research provided:
- Q1 FY2027 actual revenue: $81.6 billion (ended April 26, 2026)
- Q2 FY2027 guidance issued May 20, 2026: ~$91.0 billion ±2%
- This represents ~11.5% sequential growth from Q1 to Q2
- Wall Street consensus: $91.8 billion (with range $90.3B to $96.7B)
- LSEG average estimate: $86.84 billion (notably lower than NVIDIA's guidance)

## Analysis

The question asks "What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release?" 

This is slightly ambiguous—it could mean:
1. The forward guidance that was already given (which is $91.0B ±2%)
2. A new forward guidance for a subsequent quarter announced during Q2 FY2027 earnings

Given the phrasing and the fact that we're already past the May 20 guidance date, I interpret this as asking what the actual Q2 FY2027 revenue will be (which will be compared against the guidance of $91.0B ±2%).

The range provided (99.5B to 115.5B) is notably higher than the guidance of $91.0B ±2% or even Wall Street consensus of $91.8B. This suggests the question might be asking about a different metric or there's been a significant change in expectations.

However, taking the question at face value with the data provided:
- Guided range: $89.2B - $92.8B
- Wall Street consensus: $91.8B
- The range provided extends well above both these figures

Given that NVIDIA typically achieves or slightly exceeds guidance, and considering the strong momentum, the actual revenue is most likely to come in at or slightly above the $91.0B guidance midpoint. The provided range extends far beyond reasonable expectations based on current guidance and analyst consensus.

My estimate for actual Q2 FY2027 revenue:
- 10th percentile (likely miss to downside): $88.5B
- 50th percentile (most likely): $91.0B - $91.5B  
- 90th percentile (upside case): $94.0B

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue, released on May 20, 2026, predicts approximately $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%. This outlook explicitly excludes any Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html). This figure is well above the average quarterly revenue estimate of $86.84 billion, according to LSEG [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html).

For Q1 FY2027, which ended April 26, 2026, NVIDIA reported a record revenue of $81.6 billion, an 85% increase from the prior year and up 20% from the previous quarter [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [barchart.com](https://www.barchart.com/story/news/3449043/what-to-expect-from-nvidia-s-q2-2027-earnings-report). Wall Street analysts' consensus for Q2 FY2027 revenue is $91.8 billion, with a low estimate of $90.3 billion and a high of $96.7 billion [tickerleague.com](https://tickerleague.com/companies/NVDA/estimates).
